title: Walking a whole tree
summary: Visit every node with left, node, right recursion to get a sorted list, and measure height from the bottom up.

say.never: Finding one number only walks one path. Some jobs need **every** node: counting them, or listing them all. For that, a method handles a node by doing three things: deal with the **left** side (by calling itself), deal with **this node**, then deal with the **right** side (calling itself again). When it reaches `null` it does nothing and returns.
say.bit: To visit every node: recurse left, handle this node, recurse right. `null` does nothing.

board.code:
visit(spot):
    spot is null?  -> stop
    visit(left side)
    do something with spot
    visit(right side)

steps.title: Left, node, right comes out sorted

say.never: In a search tree, everything on the left is smaller and everything on the right is bigger. So if you write down the left side first, then the node, then the right side, the numbers come out **smallest to biggest**, every time. This order is called an **in-order** walk. You get a sorted list for free.
say.bit: An **in-order** walk (left, node, right) of a search tree visits the numbers in sorted order.

say.never: To collect the numbers, make **one** list at the top and hand that same list to every call. Each call adds its own number to it, at the right moment. Don't make a new list inside the recursive helper, or each call fills its own list and the answer gets lost.
say.bit: Create the list once and pass it into the helper; each call adds to the same list.

say.never: The **height** of a tree is how many nodes are on its longest path from the top down. Think of it as a question each node asks its two children: "how tall are you?" An empty spot (`null`) is 0 tall. A node is 1 (itself) plus whichever child is taller. `Math.max(a, b)` gives you the bigger of two numbers.
say.bit: Height: `null` is 0; a node is 1 + the taller of its two sides. Use `Math.max`.

board.code:
50          height 3
       /  \
     20    80       20 is 2 tall, 80 is 1 tall
    /
  10                10 is 1 tall

50: 1 + max(2, 1) = 3

steps.title: In your lesson: Height, from the bottom up

say.never: `inOrder()` returns an `ArrayList<Integer>`. Make the list there, hand it to a helper that walks left, node, right, then return it. `height()` is another helper that starts at `root_`. Both stop at a `null` node, so an empty tree gives an empty list and a height of 0.
say.bit: inOrder: make one list, fill it with a left/node/right helper, return it. height: a helper from `root_`, `null` is 0.
